summary: Checked the claims that drive the timeline (rate limits, Marketplace thresholds and review windows) against Slack's official docs, and re-ran the agent's probes. Everything checked held up; one open question about the managed path.

corrections.claim: Since May 29, 2025, unlisted distributed apps get 1 request/minute and 15 objects/call on conversations.history and conversations.replies
corrections.finding: Confirmed in Slack's changelog. It applies to commercially distributed apps created after that date and to net new installs of existing apps; internal (custom) apps keep 50+ req/min and 1,000 objects.

corrections.claim: Marketplace listing needs 10 active workspaces (active in last 28 days)
corrections.finding: Confirmed in the Marketplace review guide.

corrections.claim: Preliminary review up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks
corrections.finding: Confirmed (6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes).

corrections.claim: Tested: authorize endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a client-rendered error for an unknown client; OIDC discovery exists without registration_endpoint; console requires sign-in
corrections.finding: Re-ran all three probes independently on 2026-10-28 and got identical results.

corrections.claim: Composio's managed Slack app path has only shared-quota limits
corrections.finding: Unknown whether Composio's managed Slack app is Marketplace-approved, which decides if the 1 req/min history limit applies to it. Worth confirming with Composio before recommending the managed path for history-heavy agents.
